name: packed-earth yard ground autotile: tamped reddish-brown earth with faint wheel rut, footprints, pebbles and straw, a slight earth bank shadow on the south edge and grass tufts creeping over the rim, lying flat on grass (top-down 3/4 RPG ground)
label: beodeul_yard/dirt

surfaces.part: packed-earth ground plane (flat, seen from above)

answer.evidence: This is a flat ground autotile with an irregular earth patch on grass and a grass hole in the middle. The earth fills about rows 3-125, with rut, footprint, pebble and straw marks drawn straight down on it. The only south-facing element is a thin bank edge. In column x=88 a light edge line sits at rows 122-123 and a dark shadow at rows 124-125, then grass resumes. In column x=131 the same edge is at row 123 with shadow at rows 124-125. That is a 2-row lip, not a front face of 3 or more rows. No vertical face or side face is drawn, so it reads as a flat top-down slab, as expected for a terrain tile.

styleAnswer.evidence: The measured facts support the candidate. It has 9 visible tones per tile against 3 for the grass reference and 7 for the paving reference. Near-flat coverage is 3% against 0% for both references, so there are no real flat fills. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, which matches the picture: the earth rim is a dark reddish-brown beside the soil and a darker green beside the grass, not a black line. The soil has grain speckle, pebbles, straw flecks and a darker rim with a south bank shadow. Grass tufts creep over the edge, and the surrounding grass carries faint tuft marks. The soil ramp is about 4 steps (light, mid, dark, rim shadow) against 5-6 for Beodeul, and the rut and footprints are very faint. These are slight weaknesses but not a shallow or sticker look, and the tile density is at or above the references.

answer.evidence: This is a flat ground autotile seen from above. The only vertical element is a thin bank lip on the south edge: a light line at rows 122-123, then dark shadow rows 124-126 at x=88 and x=131. That is about 2-4 rows, so it is a rim and not a front face of 3 or more rows. The patch has no standing volume, so for terrain it reads as a flat top-down slab, which is the intended look for ground.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 9 visible tones per tile against 3 for the grass reference and 7 for the paving. Its near-flat coverage is 3%, close to the references' 0%, so there are no large flat fills. The 0% near-neutral dark edge share means the outline is tinted. By eye, the rim is a dark brown, earth-toned edge with grass tufts, and the south bank shadow is separated by value rather than a black line. The earth carries speckled soil grain, pebbles, straw flecks and rut or footprint marks, and the surrounding grass matches the reference's tuft texture. On the measured facts it is still at or above the references, and a careful artist would accept it beside them.

surfaces.part: packed-earth ground body (flat dirt area with ruts, footprints, pebbles, straw)
grass tufts on the rim and small detached dirt patch at top right

answer.evidence: This is a flat ground autotile seen from above. The dirt surface runs from about row 1 to row 121, with a light edge line at rows 122-123 (#ae7c50) and a thin dark bank shadow at rows 124-125 (#70502e, #4c3620). That gives only about 2 rows of bank face plus shadow, short of a 3-row front face, so there is no real vertical south face. The same 1-2 row lip and shadow repeats on the south edges of the inner grass hole (rows 24-25) and the right-hand lobe (rows 76-78). As terrain, the ground is meant to be flat and top-down, so the missing deep front face is expected.

styleAnswer.evidence: The earth patch has about 4 brown steps: a dark brown rim and south-bank shadow, a mid brown body, lighter grain flecks and darker clods. Pebbles and straw add grey and yellow dots, and grass tufts overlap the rim. The edge is a dark tinted brown, matching the 0% near-neutral edge share, so it is not a sticker-style black line. The surrounding grass has faint tufts and is a bit softer than the reference grass, but it is not a flat fill. Measured facts support this: 9 visible tones per tile against 3 for the grass reference and 7 for paving, 3% near-flat coverage, and tinted edge pixels. The earth body is somewhat uniform in places and its ramp is slightly shallower than the Beodeul 5-6 steps, but a careful artist would accept it next to the reference.
